_readme: Attacks already seen and named. Install on the Vault VM at /etc/modsec-tail/known-attacks.json (0644).
modsec-tail.py re-reads it whenever it changes: no restart. Check the journal for 'N known attacks loaded'.
A matching modsec event gets known_attack / known_cve. custom-discord pings for EVERY modsec event
whose known_attack is empty (any score), so adding an entry here is how a new attack stops pinging.
Entry: name, optional cve, and conditions in all (every one must hold), any (at least one, if listed),
none (none may hold). Condition: {"in": field, op: value}.
fields: method path query uri body body_raw host ua headers header_names rules attacks, or header:<name>
body has \uXXXX / \xNN escapes undone (attackers write __proto__ as \u005f\u005f...), body_raw is as sent.
ops:    has (substring) / re (regex) / equals (whole value), all case-insensitive; present (true/false)
First match wins: specific exploits first, the generic scan categories last.
The generic ones carry a 'none' on injection-type attacks so a real RCE / SQLi that happens to hit
a .php path or carry a scanner header still counts as new and pings.
Built from 7 days of real traffic (2026-11-11..18), then extended 2026-11-19 from the 60-day archive that
scripts/root_scripts/modsec-archive.sh keeps in /srv/logs/modsec-archive/ (~21k records, all named after that pass
except own curl tests and 2 cookie false positives). Entries marked 'not seen yet' are well-known extras.

attacks.name: React2Shell (escaped JSON, WAF evasion)
attacks.note: seen 2026-11-18: keys written as \u0074\u0068\u0065\u006e..., some with binary padding or the $ACTION_REF_ / "bound":"$@1" form; runs id via node:child_process

attacks.name: React2Shell (gzip-compressed body, WAF evasion)
attacks.note: seen 2026-11-18 from the same IPs as the escaped-JSON variant: Next-Action + Content-Encoding, gzip body (\x1f\x8b) so the WAF can't read it; ModSecurity 400s it (200002, body parse failed)

attacks.name: React2Shell (headers only, body not inspected)
attacks.note: seen 2026-11-18 23:29: POST with Next-Action + Accept: text/x-component and TWO Content-Type headers (CRS 920620, parser confusion), 14 KB body never read because dnsbl denied it in the access phase; 13 POSTs in 3 s from one IP with rotating Chrome UAs. Next-Action is Next.js Server Actions only, Vaultwarden never sends it

attacks.name: WordPress REST batch SQLi
attacks.note: seen 2026-11-18, UA 'cve-2026-63030/1.0' (CVE claimed by the tool, not verified): UNION SELECT inside a nested /wp/v2/posts request

attacks.name: PHP-CGI argument injection
attacks.note: seen 2026-10..11 (60-day archive): ?%ADd+allow_url_include=1+%ADd+auto_prepend_file=php://input (soft hyphen, or plain -d) on /index.php, /php-cgi/php-cgi.exe, /cgi-bin/php*, PHP body running shell_exec('env') and cat'ing .env / AWS creds

attacks.name: Langflow code-validation RCE
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-01 in the env-secret campaign: POST /api/v1/validate/code (also under /langflow/), Python in the body

attacks.name: Langflow public-flow build
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-01 in the env-secret campaign: POST /api/v1/build_public_tmp/<flow id>/flow, code injection through an unauthenticated public flow

attacks.name: Flowise CustomMCP RCE
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-01 in the env-secret campaign: POST /api/v1/node-load-method/customMCP (also under /flowise/), JS in the MCP config

attacks.name: Spring Cloud Function routing RCE
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-01: POST /functionRouter and /api/functionRouter, text/plain body 'test' (a probe, the payload normally rides in spring.cloud.function.routing-expression)

attacks.name: Laravel Ignition RCE
attacks.note: seen 2026-10..11: GET /_ignition/execute-solution from the Accept-Charset scanner, checking whether the endpoint exists

attacks.name: Env-secret file read
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-01, one campaign trying every hole for the process environment (cloud keys, tokens): Feast /feast/read-document {"file_path":"/proc/self/environ"}, Vite RSC ?filename=file:///proc/self/environ, Next.js bypass + ?path=../../proc/self/environ on /api/fs/read, /api/system/fileView, /userfiles, Kibana's /api/console/api_server?apis=../ (CVE-2018-17246), GET /process.env, {"templateFile":"../../../../.env"}. Runs after the React2Shell entries, so their own secret dump keeps its name

attacks.name: GraphQL introspection probe
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-11: POST /graphql asking for __schema (the API's full type list, step one of a GraphQL attack). CRS reads the JSON braces as SQLi. No GraphQL here

attacks.name: phpinfo scan
attacks.note: seen 2026-09-22: GET /cgi-bin/phpinfo.php with itself as referer (the referer trips CRS's file-access + shell rules, so the PHP webshell entry's guard skips it)

attacks.name: WordPress install finder (double slash)
attacks.note: seen 2026-09-30 and 10-26: GET //xmlrpc.php?rsd, //blog/, //wordpress/, //wp/, //blog/robots.txt in a burst, referer some other site's //wp-login.php, carrying that site's cookies (LSKey-c$CookieConsentPolicy, ...). The RCE / SQLi matches are CRS false positives on those COOKIES, not a payload. 404 here

attacks.name: Python exec endpoint probe
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-01 in the env-secret campaign: POST /exec-py, code=<base64 Python running env / cat /proc/self/environ>. 404 here, no such endpoint

attacks.name: ALFA webshell scan
attacks.note: seen 2026-10..11: POST //alfacgiapi/perl.alfa and //ALFA_DATA/alfacgiapi/perl.alfa, looking for an already-planted ALFA webshell's CGI helper. 404 here

attacks.name: RootEvidence research scanner
attacks.note: self-identified scanner (RootEvidence/1.0, Opt-Out-Email / Opt-Out-Url headers), GET / only

attacks.name: Secret-file scan (unexpanded $(pwd))
attacks.note: seen 2026-11-22, four IPs in one /24 at the same second, ~1000 secret-file GETs between them (.env, .aws/credentials, terraform.tfstate ...), fake Chrome 131. Some paths kept a literal '$(pwd)/' the scanner's wordlist never expanded (/$(pwd)/docker-compose.yml, /$(pwd)/.terraform/terraform.tfstate). CRS 932239 (PL2) reads '$(pwd)' as shell command substitution, so the Secret-file scan entry's 'no rce' guard skips them. DNSBL had them 403'd anyway

attacks.name: Secret-file scan
attacks.note: 930121 added 2026-11-19: the file name in a header (GET /app/config/parameters.yml with itself as referer)

attacks.name: Go-client binary POST probe
attacks.note: seen 2026-11 from Go-http-client/1.1 and /2.0, cookie set, header order content-type,content-length,accept-encoding,user-agent,cookie,host: POST with an opaque binary or empty body and a rotating disallowed content type (application/octet-stream, audio/x-wav, ...). Purpose unknown

attacks.name: Opaque-cookie POST probe (no User-Agent)
attacks.note: seen 2026-11-19 on plain http to the apex: same shape as the Go-client probe but NO User-Agent (920320), header order host,content-length,content-type,cookie,accept-encoding. POST / with Content-Type multipart/alternative (920420, so CRS never reads the ~6 KB body), a long base64 cookie 'sesskeyapiv2'. Nothing public on that cookie name. Got the http->https 301 only. Purpose unknown

attacks.name: Opaque-cookie POST probe (rotating UAs)
attacks.note: seen 2026-09..11: the same family as the two above with browser UAs (IE11, iPhone, Android, old Chrome): POST / with a cookie, a disallowed content type (octet-stream, xhtml+xml, text/csv, 920420) or no UA (920320), random binary or empty body. Purpose unknown

attacks.name: Method-override / IP-spoofing probe
attacks.note: seen 2026-11-04..11: X-HTTP-Method-Override / X-Method-Override plus a pile of forged client-IP headers (CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP ... random or 127.0.0.1) on GET /?rest_route=/ (WordPress REST discovery). Tries to look like an internal or allowlisted caller

attacks.name: Content-Type on a GET
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-11: GET / with Content-Type text/html (920420), old Chrome/74 UA. A broken bot, not an attack

attacks.name: Fake Googlebot
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-22: UA 'Googlebot/2.1 +http://www.googlebot.com/bot.html' (Google's real UA points to google.com) with a malformed 'Accept: */*,' (920600)

attacks.name: Unfilled-template crawler UA
attacks.note: seen 2026-11-20: 'PageHubBot/1.0; +https://[DOMAIN]/bot', the bot's author never filled in the placeholder. CRS 932131 (PL2, 'Unix shell expression') reads '/[domain]' as shell syntax, so it scores 5: 301 on http, 403 on https since blocking went to PL2. GET / on the apex only. A false positive on a junk crawler, blocking it costs nothing

attacks.name: Bare POST probe (1=1)
attacks.note: seen 2026-10-08: POST / with body '1=1' and no Content-Type (920340 + 920640)

attacks.name: Accept-Charset scanner
attacks.note: seen 2026-10..11, ~55 hits: old-style 'Accept-Charset: utf-8' header (920451, restricted header, score 0) on /, /robots.txt, /favicon.ico, appsettings.json ..., rotating Windows / Nokia / MeeGo UAs. Real browsers stopped sending Accept-Charset years ago

attacks.name: Backup-archive scan
attacks.note: seen 2026-10..11, ~100 hits: GET /backup.zip, /db.tar.gz, /www.rar, /cookiefamily.zip, /dump.7z ... no User-Agent, a Range header (grab the start of a big file). Plain http, got the 301 only

attacks.name: No-User-Agent path scan
attacks.note: seen 2026-10..11, ~110 hits: GET / HEAD with no User-Agent at all (920320 only, score 0) for WordPress folders, .php7 / .phP8 shells, Cloudflare-Worker relayed GET /. Mostly plain http, got the 301 only. After the specific entries, so a named exploit sent without a UA keeps its name
